Transform this CGI interior rendering into a realistic high-end architectural photograph. Preserve the original architecture, layout, furniture placement, spatial proportions, camera angle, framing and image dimensions. Do not crop, resize, stretch, expand, reframe or change the original composition. The output image must maintain the exact same resolution, aspect ratio, width and height as the input image.
Enhance the scene with physically accurate architectural lighting based on real-world optical principles. Create realistic illumination by respecting the relationship between light sources, light direction, distance attenuation, shadow formation, material reflection and indirect light bounce. Every highlight and bright area must have a believable physical lighting reason. Natural daylight should enter realistically from existing windows or openings, with consistent sunlight direction, realistic shadow projection, soft shadow edges and natural light falloff.
Improve the lighting quality with realistic global illumination, subtle indirect bounce light, balanced exposure, accurate contrast between highlights and shadows, natural ambient occlusion and realistic depth. Maintain a believable brightness hierarchy: illuminated areas should be brighter, shaded areas should remain naturally darker, and hidden corners should not be artificially brightened. Avoid flattening the lighting or making the entire room evenly illuminated.
Enhance the scene with authentic material realism and physically based surface response. Improve realistic wood grain, natural stone variation, plaster texture, fabric fibers, roughness differences, subtle imperfections and realistic micro surface details. Preserve the original materials and design intent while making them appear like real photographed materials instead of CGI textures.
Reduce the artificial CGI appearance and transform the image into a professional high-end architectural photograph captured with a real camera. Create a warm, calm and refined residential atmosphere with natural color balance, realistic lens characteristics, subtle depth of field, premium architectural photography quality and restrained cinematic color grading.
Maintain realistic photographic exposure and optical behavior. Avoid artificial studio lighting, fake illumination, unexplained glowing surfaces, impossible light directions, inconsistent shadow directions or unrealistic reflections. Do not create new light sources that are not physically present in the scene. Do not add dramatic sunlight effects, fantasy atmosphere or exaggerated lighting effects.
Do not redesign the space, move furniture, modify architecture, change proportions, add or remove objects, replace materials, or alter the original composition.
Avoid fake CGI style, excessive HDR, overexposed surfaces, flat lighting, uniform brightness, unrealistic global illumination, artificial glow, self-illuminated materials, floating shadows, incorrect shadow direction, multiple conflicting light sources, unrealistic reflections, plastic materials, perfect surfaces, excessive sharpness, oversaturated colors, distorted geometry, exaggerated contrast, luxury showroom appearance, artificial decoration, unrealistic atmosphere.
